Let $\mathcal C$ be an additive $\mathbb C$-linear rigid monoidal category with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1)=\mathbb C$, and fix a pivotal structure $j_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ as in [[def-pivotal-structure]]. For $f:X\to Y$, call $f$ **negligible** if

$$\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_X\circ g\circ f)=0\qquad\text{for every }g:Y\to X,$$

where the left trace is [[def-the-categorical-trace-of-a-morphism-into-the-double-dual]]. The negligible morphisms form the intersection of the kernels of these linear functionals; this definition alone does not assert tensor-ideal closure.

For the complex Temperley–Lieb diagram category, use its cup/cap pivotal structure. The resulting trace is exactly the unnormalized planar closure of [[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]]. The same definition applies to the complex type-1 tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]] when its stated ribbon pivotal structure is used.

Let $(-)^{\vee\vee}$ be the monoidal endofunctor of
[[thm-the-double-dual-is-a-monoidal-functor]].

A **pivotal structure** on a rigid monoidal category is an isomorphism of
monoidal functors

$$a:\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{\sim}(-)^{\vee\vee}.$$

Equivalently, it is a natural family of isomorphisms
$a_X:X\xrightarrow{\sim}X^{\vee\vee}$ such that

$$a_{X\otimes Y}=a_X\otimes a_Y,\qquad a_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$$

after transporting along the monoidal structure of the double-dual functor.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a rigid monoidal category, let $a:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ and $b:Y\to Y^{\vee\vee}$, and suppress the monoidal and chosen-dual comparison maps. For $s\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)$ write $\ell_Z(s)$ and $r_Z(s)$ for its left and right actions on $Z$, transported from $s\otimes1_Z$ and $1_Z\otimes s$ by the unit constraints.

1. $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(a^\vee)$.
2. If the category is additive, then
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\oplus b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)+\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
3. The general tensor formula is
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))a)$.
   If $r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))=\ell_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))$, this becomes
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
   In particular multiplicativity holds when every unit scalar has equal left and right actions on every object. This condition holds in a braided category, and also in a $k$-linear monoidal category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$.
4. For every endomorphism $c:X\to X$,
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(ac)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(c^{\vee\vee}a)$.

The corresponding right-trace duality, additivity and cyclicity statements hold. For right-trace inputs $p:X^{\vee\vee}\to X$ and $q:Y^{\vee\vee}\to Y$, the general tensor formula is

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(p\otimes q)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(q\ell_{Y^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_R(p))).$$

It reduces to multiplicativity under the analogous equality of scalar actions, in particular under either sufficient condition above.

An object of a monoidal category is **rigid** if it has both a left dual and a
right dual in the sense of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]].

A monoidal category is **rigid** if every object in it is rigid.

Muger's notes also use the word **autonomous** for the same condition, and
Joyal-Street use **compact** in the non-symmetric setting.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\delta\in R$, and use the noncrossing-pairing diagram category of [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]], with the left factor stacked above the right factor. For a basis diagram $D:n\to n$, close each top endpoint to the corresponding bottom endpoint outside the rectangle and let $c(D)$ be the number of circles in the resulting finite graph. Define

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(D)=\delta^{c(D)}$$

and extend $R$-linearly to $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$. This is the **unnormalized closure trace**. In particular, $\operatorname{Tr}_0(1_0)=1$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_n(1_n)=\delta^n$. No unit or nonzero condition on $\delta$ is required.

Let $\cup:0\to2$ and $\cap:2\to0$ be the standard cup and cap in the diagram category. For $n\ge1$ define the **right partial trace** by

$$\operatorname{ptr}_n(x)=(1_{n-1}\otimes\cap)\circ(x\otimes1_1)\circ(1_{n-1}\otimes\cup),\qquad x\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta).$$

It is a map $\mathrm{TL}_n\to\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}$. If $\delta$ is a unit, define $\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. This agrees with the normalized trace of [[def-temperley-lieb-normalized-markov-trace-by-closure]] over $\mathbb C$ when $\delta\ne0$.

For any commutative ring $R$, loop value $\delta\in R$, and $n\ge0$, the unnormalized trace of [[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]] satisfies

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(xy)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(yx),\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}(x\otimes1)=\delta\operatorname{Tr}_n(x)$$

for $x,y\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$. For $n\ge1$ and $x\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$, it also satisfies

$$\operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}((x\otimes1)U_n)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(x),$$

where $U_n$ is the cup-cap generator on the last two strands of $\mathrm{TL}_{n+1}$. For $n\ge1$, $x\in\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}$ and $h\in\mathrm{TL}_n$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n\bigl(h(x\otimes1)\bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}_{n-1}\bigl(\operatorname{ptr}_n(h)x\bigr).$$

No division by $\delta$ occurs.

For $h:Z\otimes Y\to Z\otimes X$ define $\widetilde{\operatorname{coev}}_Z=(1_{Z^\vee}\otimes j_Z^{-1})\operatorname{coev}_{Z^\vee}:\mathbf1\to Z^\vee\otimes Z$ and $\operatorname{ptr}^{L}_Z(h)=(\operatorname{ev}_Z\otimes1_X)(1_{Z^\vee}\otimes h)(\widetilde{\operatorname{coev}}_Z\otimes1_Y):Y\to X$. For any $g:Z\to W$, $f\otimes g=(1_Y\otimes g)(f\otimes1_Z)$ and $g\otimes f=(g\otimes1_Y)(1_Z\otimes f)$. Composition closure from step 1.1 and the two partial-trace arguments in steps 2.1 and 2.2 therefore give closure under tensoring on either side by arbitrary morphisms. In the Temperley–Lieb category, [L1] also verifies the partial-trace identities by counting components of the closed finite stacked graph. Together with linearity this proves tensor-ideal closure.

$$\operatorname{ptr}_n(p_n)=\frac{[n+1]}{[n]}p_{n-1},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(p_n)=[n+1].$$

Only the displayed denominator units are assumed; $\delta$ need not be a unit.

where $U_n$ is the cup-cap generator on the last two strands of $\mathrm{TL}_{n+1}$. For $n\ge1$, $x\in\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}$ and $h\in\mathrm{TL}_n$,

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and let $\delta\in R$. The object labels are the nonnegative integers $n=0,1,2,\ldots$. For labels $m,n$, place bottom points $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ and top points $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ along the rectangle from left to right on their respective edges. Their cyclic order is $t_1,\ldots,t_n,b_m,\ldots,b_1$. When $m=n=0$, the empty matching is included.

An $(m,n)$ **diagram** is a perfect matching of these $m+n$ boundary labels which is noncrossing: there are no four labels $a,b,c,d$ in cyclic order whose matched pairs are $\{a,c\}$ and $\{b,d\}$. A picture consists of disjoint arcs realizing the matching; equality is equality of the matching, so planar deformation that fixes the boundary does not change a diagram. If $m+n$ is odd, there are no such diagrams. Write $\mathcal D(m,n)$ for this set and define the $R$-module

$$M_R(m,n):=R^{(\mathcal D(m,n))},$$

the free $R$-module on the set of diagrams ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]). In particular, its diagram basis is empty when $m+n$ is odd.

For basis diagrams $D:m\to n$ and $E:n\to p$, stack $E$ above $D$ and identify the $n$ matching boundary points. The resulting finite graph has degree two at each identified point, where degree means the number of incident arcs. Each component is a path joining two exterior boundary points or a closed cycle. Remove every cycle and multiply the remaining exterior matching by $\delta^c$, where $c$ is the number of removed cycles. Denote this output by $E\circ D$ and extend the rule $R$-bilinearly to a map $M_R(n,p)\times M_R(m,n)\to M_R(m,p)$. A following result proves closure of these operations on the diagram modules and the category axioms.

The matching $1_n:n\to n$ pairs each bottom point to the top point directly above it.
